chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Al-Hasan, from Zur'ah, from Sama'ah, who said:

I asked him about a man who performs salat (prayer) and recites the Qur'an while he is covering his mouth with a cloth. He said: “There is no harm in it, but if he uncovers his mouth, then that is better.”

He said: And I asked him about a woman who performs salat (prayer) while wearing a face veil. He said: “If she uncovers the place of sajdah (prostration), then there is no harm in it, but if she uncovers her face, then that is better.”

Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, said: It is not permissible for a man to perform salat (prayer) while a woman is performing salat (prayer) beside him or in the same row. Whenever he prays while she is directly aligned with him in his row, both of their prayers are invalid. If it happens that she performs her salat (prayer) at the same time as his in one house or the like, she should pray in such a way that her place of sajdah (prostration) is opposite his feet while he is in his sajdah (prostration). Likewise, if she performs salat (prayer) following his salat (prayer), her state should be as we have described.

key_terms.أَفْضَلُ: better and more preferable in practice
key_terms.سُجُودُهَا: her act or place of prostration in prayer
key_terms.صَفٍّ وَاحِدٍ: a single row in congregational or parallel prayer formation
key_terms.مَوْضِعِ اَلسُّجُودِ: the area of prostration that should remain uncovered
key_terms.مُتَلَثِّمٌ: covering the mouth with a cloth during salat (prayer)
key_terms.مُتَنَقِّبَةً: wearing a face veil during salat (prayer)
key_terms.مُسَامِتَةٌ: directly aligned beside another in the same row

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to perform salat (prayer) while covering the mouth or face, and how should a man and woman be positioned when praying together?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses legal rulings related to salat (prayer) while the mouth or face is covered. It states that praying in such a state is permissible, though uncovering is better, and it also includes a juristic ruling from Al-Shaykh concerning the positioning of a man and woman when praying at the same time.
